_about: Verified news items, newest first. Each needs a date (YYYY-MM-DD), a plain-language summary, at least one source, and optionally the therapy id from therapies.json. Include setbacks as well as good news.

items.title: NPI-001 Phase 3 trial doses its first patient
items.summary: Nacuity's twice-daily tablet for RP caused by Usher syndrome began its 2-year confirmatory trial. It will enroll up to 80 adults in the US and Australia.

items.title: Laru-zova meets its main goal in X-linked RP
items.summary: In Beacon's pivotal VISTA trial, 31% of high-dose patients gained at least 3 lines of dim-light reading vision after a year, versus none of the untreated group. It is the first X-linked RP trial to succeed.

items.title: FDA accepts application for MCO-010 (MOGENRY)
items.summary: The FDA will review Nanoscope's gene-agnostic optogenetic therapy for RP with severe vision loss. A decision is expected in the first half of 2027.

items.title: RTx-015 gets RMAT status from the FDA
items.summary: The designation gives Ray Therapeutics' optogenetic therapy closer FDA guidance and a possible faster review. No efficacy data have been published yet.

items.title: OCU400 Phase 3 finishes enrolling 140 people
items.summary: Ocugen's gene-agnostic gene therapy trial includes children aged 3 and up. First results are expected in early 2027.

items.title: Bota-vec Phase 3 misses its main goal
items.summary: The LUMEOS trial of this RPGR gene therapy did not improve the maze-navigation test it was judged on, though some other vision measures improved.
